elements.element: Licence/access rights extend to Customer's affiliates
elements.evidence: extend to the Company's affiliates (each entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with the Company)

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: and to contractors acting on the Company's behalf
No paid-up licence exists in this hosting access clause; condition absent. The inserted text nonetheless confirms 'Such rights are not revocable at HDI's discretion'

elements.element: Subscription/term rights terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: may be suspended or withdrawn only for a material breach by the Company that remains uncured thirty (30) days after written notice
transferable to any successor to all or substantially all of the Company's business or assets by merger, acquisition or sale
extend to the Company's affiliates ... (granted outright, a superset of notice-conditioned coverage)

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: transferable to any successor ... by merger, acquisition or sale

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present in the single inserted sub-section: affiliate extension with a control-based definition, contractors acting on Customer's behalf, a no-at-will-revocation/uncured-material-breach limit with a 30-day cure, and successor transferability by merger, acquisition or sale.

The perpetual/irrevocable paid-up element is conditional and its condition is absent — Section 1.4 grants hosting access rights under the term of the Agreement, not a paid-up licence — so no perpetual grant needed to be invented.
Minimality holds: one concise insertion completes an absent scope provision; the original two sentences on system access, bandwidth, burst capacity and administration tools are untouched.
The carve-out 'or upon expiration or termination of this Agreement' preserves the existing term structure rather than adding a new exception, so no dangling mechanic or contradiction is introduced.
